title: Microsoft Teams: separate attendance and engagement report policy for Teams events
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned events control from the existing meeting control and reports Microsoft's rollout window and default correctly. The documented commands, admin paths and report licensing statements are supported; the remaining gaps are appropriately identified as unpublished.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Microsoft plans separate attendance and engagement report controls for Teams events and Teams meetings.
claims.quote: Teams events will soon have a separate attendance and engagement report policy from the "CsTeamsMeetingPolicy" attendance and engagement report policy.

claims.claim: The new setting is in CsTeamsEventsPolicy, while meeting reporting remains managed through CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.
claims.quote: administrators can independently manage organizer access to attendance and engagement reports for Teams Events through CsTeamsEventsPolicy, without affecting attendance and engagement report settings for Teams Meetings managed through CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.

claims.claim: Administrators can configure event report access independently of meeting report access.
claims.quote: This update provides greater administrative flexibility by allowing separate configuration of attendance and engagement reporting for Teams Events and Teams Meetings.

claims.claim: MC1455014 was updated on 3 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: An assigned custom events policy takes the place of the global policy for that user.
claims.quote: You can edit the settings in the global policy or create and assign one or more custom policies. Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one events policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot view attendance and engagement reports for events they did not organise.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can’t view the attendance and engagement report for meetings and events that you didn't organize.

claims.quote: However, you can view attendees' details for a given meeting or event within 24 hours of that meeting or event.

claims.quote: go to Users > Manage users. Choose the display name for the meeting organizer. Select the Meetings & calls tab, and then choose the appropriate meeting ID or call ID. Then, select Participant details.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport ForceDisabled blocks event report viewing and downloading.
claims.quote:
-Identity
Unique identifier assigned to the Teams Events policy.
-AllowEngagementReport
Controls whether attendance and engagement reports are allowed for events.
ForceDisabled: Off. Organizers cannot view or download attendance and engagement reports.

Grant-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity "user1@contoso.com" -Policy DisablePublicWebinars

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport Disabled turns off reports under the existing meeting policy.

To turn off attendance and engagement reports, use the following script:
